name: Fort Zeelandia, Paramaribo
name_zh: 帕拉马里博 · 泽兰迪亚堡
note: 1663 年前后，年轻的阿芙拉·贝恩在当时还是英国殖民地的苏里南住过几个月，后来写成《奥鲁诺可》：一位被骗卖为奴的非洲王子在苏里南的种植园里领导奴隶起义。这是英语里最早的小说之一，书里她还惋惜国王把这片“永远是春天”的土地拱手让给了荷兰——1667 年英国用苏里南换来了新阿姆斯特丹，也就是后来的纽约。这座要塞原是英国人的威洛比堡，荷兰人攻占后改名泽兰迪亚。伏尔泰的老实人也到过这里，在城外遇见一个被砍去手脚的奴隶，听他说出“你们在欧洲吃的糖，就是这个代价”。要塞今天是苏里南博物馆
note_en: Around 1663 the young Aphra Behn spent a few months in Surinam, then an English colony, and later wrote Oroonoko, the story of an African prince tricked into slavery who leads a slave revolt on a Surinam plantation. It is one of the earliest novels in English, and in it she laments that the king gave away this land of 'eternal Spring' to the Dutch: in 1667 England traded Surinam for New Amsterdam, which became New York. The fort was built by the English as Fort Willoughby and renamed Zeelandia when the Dutch took it. Voltaire's Candide comes here too, and outside the town meets a maimed slave who tells him, 'This is the price at which you eat sugar in Europe.' The fort is now the Surinaams Museum
